note: Original drafts with historical curriculum scope and separately registered authoritative fact checks. Current adoption, paper-level scope and four-option convention remain provisional.

questions.subject: History
questions.learningObjective: Identify when Northern and Southern Nigeria were amalgamated.
questions.prompt: A museum timeline has a space for the joining of Northern and Southern Nigeria into the Colony and Protectorate of Nigeria. Which year belongs in that space?
questions.explanation: The National Archives dates the amalgamation of the Northern and Southern protectorates to 1914.

questions.subject: History
questions.learningObjective: Identify the date on which Nigeria attained independence.
questions.prompt: A class is preparing a display about the end of British governmental responsibility for Nigeria. Which date marks Nigeria’s independence?
options: 1 January 1914
1 October 1960
1 October 1963
questions.explanation: Section 1 of the Nigeria Independence Act 1960 specifies 1 October 1960 as the appointed day.

questions.subject: History
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish independence from the later adoption of republican status.
questions.prompt: A learner writes that Nigeria first became independent when it became a republic in 1963. Which correction is accurate?
options: Nigeria became a republic before amalgamation.
Nigeria remained under British governmental control until 1999.
Nigeria became independent in 1960 and a republic in 1963.
Independence and republican status both began in 1914.
questions.answer: Nigeria became independent in 1960 and a republic in 1963.
questions.explanation: The National Archives distinguishes independence in 1960 from the Federal Republic in 1963.

questions.subject: History
questions.learningObjective: Identify Frederick Lugard in the history of amalgamation.
questions.prompt: The National Library of Nigeria catalogues a documentary record containing a report by Sir Frederick Lugard on the amalgamation of Northern and Southern Nigeria. Which name should a pupil use when identifying this administrator?
options: Herbert Macaulay
Anthony Enahoro
Nnamdi Azikiwe
Frederick Lugard
questions.explanation: The National Library catalogue identifies Sir Frederick Lugard. The historical curriculum’s spelling Lord Laggard is erroneous.

questions.subject: History
questions.learningObjective: Describe the Berlin Conference as establishing a colonial framework rather than drawing all borders.
questions.prompt: Which statement best matches the German Foreign Office archive’s account of the Berlin Conference of 1884–1885?
options: It established rules for trade, navigation and colonial claims without drawing specific borders.
It granted Nigeria independence from Britain.
It drew every present-day African national boundary.
It elected Nigerian representatives to a new parliament.
questions.answer: It established rules for trade, navigation and colonial claims without drawing specific borders.
questions.explanation: The archival explanation distinguishes the framework agreed at Berlin from subsequent territorial developments.

questions.subject: History
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish a colonial-powers agreement from African political consent.
questions.prompt: Why would it be misleading to describe the Berlin Conference agreements as decisions freely made by African peoples?
options: The conference occurred after Nigerian independence.
African representatives were not consulted in the conference process.
The conference took place in Nigeria.
All participating states were African kingdoms.
questions.answer: African representatives were not consulted in the conference process.
questions.explanation: The German Foreign Office archive states that African representatives were not consulted. Agreement among colonial powers cannot establish African consent.
